top_signal.title: How I took my tiny startup bookkeeping firm from 4 clients to 61 in 12 months
top_signal.summary: year ago, it was me and one part time accountant doing books for 4 startup clients. all from friends. good ones too. but referrals just stopped, and i had no idea how to find more without spending money i didn't have.   quick thing before anyone asks. We not a big firm. it's 3 of us. no huge marketing budget, no crazy growth plan. we just got better at finding the right people and quit doing everything manually.   my dumbest early move was cold emailing every startup i could find. the whole hey need help with your books thing. nobody replied. and honestly i get it, nobody thinks about bookkeeping until something goes wrong.   so i flipped it. started noticing when founders actually feel the pain. a founder says they just closed a round. someone's complaining their books are a mess right before tax season. someone's asking a finance post how people handle payroll. those people need help. a random startup on a list doesn't.   didn't pitch them though. i'd mention what they posted and ask one question. like congrats on the round, are you still doing the books yourself or has someone taken that over. that's it. worked way better than a cold email, no comparison.   also stopped doing the prospecting by hand. started using tools to find the right founders, reach out, follow up. before that i was losing whole days just searching for leads. now there's a steady flow instead of me sitting around waiting for a referral.   then onboarding. used to be two weeks of emails back and forth w
